pure-announcement.rationale: It is a research-results writeup with transferable findings about running autonomous research agents, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The existing weak-to-strong-generalization and automated-w2s-sandbox concepts cover the problem framing and the environment but not this note's new material: the AAR-vs-human results, the seeding and scaffolding lessons, and the evaluation-bottleneck implication.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims link to the full alignment-blog writeup and publicly released code and datasets on GitHub, so a reader can check them.

durability.rationale: The note's spine is point-in-time results — PGR 0.97 vs a 0.23 human baseline, $22 per AAR-hour, Opus 4.6 on specific Qwen pairs — which will be superseded quickly, even though the seeding and oversight lessons age better.

actionability.rationale: It gives explicit build guidance for anyone running automated research agents: seed each agent with a distinct vague direction, avoid prescriptive workflows, stress-test discovered ideas on held-out datasets, and make evaluations tamper-proof.

atomicity.rationale: Everything in the note serves one statable idea — parallel, diversely seeded autonomous agents can already do outcome-gradable alignment research, shifting the bottleneck to evaluation — rather than bundling unrelated topics.
